files.name: perps.py
files.title: perps
files.summary: Jupiter-Perps-style borrow fees, margin, and liquidation. The one thing to get right about this venue: it charges a **borrow fee**, not a funding rate. No position is ever paid to stay open.

files.name: autoreload.js
files.title: autoreload
files.summary: Auto-reload on update, as a pure decision with injected effects. Once a minute the service worker asks the soltui host for `buildHash`, a SHA-256 over the manifest and src/ of the extension directory on disk. When that hash differs from the one the worker stored, the code on disk is newer than the code Chrome loaded, and `chrome.runtime.reload()` picks it up. A reload kills the worker.

files.name: engine.js
files.title: engine
files.summary: The tick. Order of operations is the whole design: RECONCILE before PLAN, always. A MV3 service worker can be killed at any moment, including between "write the intent" and "the venue accepted the order". So the venue's live order list — not our local records — is the source of truth at the top of every tick. Local state is a cache and a journal, nothing more.

files.name: pnl.js
files.title: pnl
files.summary: P&L accounting. Two lot-matching modes, because two consumers want different answers: PAIRED (default) A sell fill that records the lots its intent was paired with (`closesLots`) closes THOSE lots. Grid exits are placed one rung above a specific buy, so when rung B's exit fills before rung A's, the inventory still held is A's, and strict FIFO would instead consume A and leave B behind.

files.summary: Tests for the Docs tab's editing guards. The load-bearing assertions are the refusals: a file under `research/results/` or not in the catalogue must never be writable, regardless of what the caller claims about it. Those are the properties a UI bug could silently violate, so they are asserted directly rather than left to code review.

files.title: test_docs_search

The memory claim is the point: the keyword postings, the embedding matrix and the ~670 MB embedding model must not be loaded until someone searches, and must be releasable. Ollama and the idle indexer are patched out; nothing here embeds anything or starts a process.

files.title: test_liquidity

Fixtures follow `liquidity/STATE_FILES.md`. The load-bearing test is `test_every_percentage_column_carries_a_source_word`: a bare "+4.6%" under a header with no source reads as "my money is up".

files.title: test_panes

That is the same split the rest of this package keeps: `tui.py` is presentation, and the logic lives in modules that can be tested without an event loop. The two worth reading first are `test_a_below_floor_row_is_never_rankable` and `test_slicing_happens_before_the_replay`.

files.name: test_signals.py
files.title: test_signals
files.summary: Tests for editable signal parameters. The load-bearing property: **an explicit per-entry parameter always beats a signal default.** Getting that direction backwards would mean the Signals tab silently overwrites a value the user deliberately pinned in the Strategies tab, and the symptom would be a strategy quietly not doing what its own label says.

files.name: test_status_roster.py
files.title: test_status_roster
files.summary: Tests for the pure soltui layer: indicator title, settings, roster, replay. The load-bearing assertion in this file is that **no money figure in the menu-bar title is ever unlabelled**. A naked '+9.4%' in a status bar reads as a live account balance, and there is no live account. That property is asserted directly rather than left to code review.

files.name: test_strategy_history.py
files.title: test_strategy_history
files.summary: The Strategies tab's test history and its three Backtest buttons. History is derived from the background sweep's results file, so what it can get wrong is counting and choosing: a duplicate line counted as a second test, a best-of-many row shown as "the" result, an untestable strategy shown as merely untested, a button that starts a sweep that has nothing to do. Each test targets one of those.
